lines: Think of the last prompt you typed twice. PromptVault gives it a home.
Could an editable decision brief earn five more first saves per hundred visitors?
This is control. The editor starts blank.
Flagsmith assigned this visitor to guided templates.
Watch the visitor ID as I refresh. Same ID, same starting experience.
I'll name this decision brief and save it.
The trace shows Flagsmith acknowledged the onboarding exposure and the first successful save under one visitor ID.
I can use fresh release notes in my saved prompt.
The Markdown export keeps the template and leaves these notes in my browser.
In a second browser, a teammate can review and import that exact template.
Import fills the draft. They still choose whether to save.
This demo sends a hundred synthetic visitors through a separate client.
Their save probabilities are programmed. The receipt counts accepted events.
To invite real people, I check a separate research environment and copy its participant link.
They see the workspace without judge controls.
Here are the filming environment's warehouse results.
Read each arm's exposure count before the lift. The inspector also has a dated, verifiable run.
In the recorded example, control saved 28 out of 145. Guided saved 41 out of 156.
That is 36 percent relative lift, with an 89 percent chance of beating control.
The interval stretches from 22 percent worse to 94 percent better. Every visitor was scripted. The measurement works. The human question stays open.
